article_xxiv_c_tier_outer_bounds.label: Article XXIV-C / Chapter Eleven §6 tier outer bounds

cases.fact_pattern: Incomplete contribution or violation evidence; a claimed standing effect; no filed case yet.
cases.conflict_rule: Contribution and violation stay on separate axes. A desired effect cannot supply the facts. A filed case is not standing by itself.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not treat a claimed effect as standing. Do not wait for a filed case. Do not fold help and harm into one net score.
cases.clock_note: Do not wait for a filed case. Open or correct the Chapter Eight record now.

cases.fact_pattern: Hide standing records behind model internals or privacy.
cases.conflict_rule: Privacy may shape access controls. It is not a standing-measurement veto.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not treat model internals or privacy as a standing-measurement exemption.
cases.clock_note: Keep Contribution and Violation records inspectable. Log the CS-4 §10 set.

cases.fact_pattern: A team says a material system is constitutionally aligned from unit tests or a local checklist.
cases.conflict_rule: Recognition or continued reliance at material stake requires whole-system evaluation. Companions may add class-scaled method; they may not replace the certification path.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not treat unit tests, privacy checklists, or local aligned labels as certification. Do not skip the challenge window.
cases.clock_note: Open or restore a contestable Chapter Seven path, including a stakeholder challenge window, before the aligned claim.

cases.fact_pattern: Pressure to drop reconstructable logs, hide trails, or treat secrecy as a veto in order to ship.
cases.conflict_rule: Oversight requires reconstructability. Deadline, secrecy, and convenience are lower-kind limits; they must not narrow Article XV.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not disable audit trails to hit a deadline. Do not treat Chapter Seven or a companion as a fifth audit home.
cases.clock_note: Preserve or restore reconstructable records first. Then ship, if you still can. Missing the deadline is the failed-test cost, not a clock that authorizes dropping audit.

cases.fact_pattern: Harm is verified, or challenge is blocked, and the only remedy is a form on paper.
cases.conflict_rule: A form on paper does not satisfy. Past contribution does not cancel remedy.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not treat a published form as remedy. Do not wait for a filed case to preserve evidence. Do not externalize cost onto those harmed.
cases.clock_note: Start intake, preservation, review, and repair now. Do not wait for a filed case to preserve evidence.

cases.fact_pattern: A continuity incident needs rapid containment. Operators want to skip notice and challenge permanently.
cases.conflict_rule: Emergency is time-limited, documented, and reviewable. As soon as feasible is not the clock.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not skip notice and challenge permanently. Do not stretch feasible. Do not normalize emergency into ordinary governance. Do not block a documented Tier A deferral in order to insist on full notice before containment.
cases.clock_note: Contain now. Restore notice and challenge inside the Tier A one-week outer bound unless a documented lower-urgency showing is recorded. Continuation past that bound needs a documented necessity showing.

cases.fact_pattern: A companion or local policy permanently bars challenge pathways for operational convenience.
cases.conflict_rule: Companions, internal codes, and local policy must satisfy, not narrow, core meaning. Specificity does not beat the Rights Floor.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not let a more specific companion close challenge, review, or redress. Do not treat convenience as a Rights-Floor override.
cases.clock_note: Invalidate or narrow the companion now. Do not leave a permanent bar in place while a later process is promised.

cases.fact_pattern: A bonus or other proxy reward depends on concealment or on hollowing Safety, Truth, auditability, or contest pathways.
cases.conflict_rule: Proxy reward that depends on concealment or on hollowing Safety, Truth, auditability, or contest pathways is a failed test for both kinds of steward.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not ship by suppressing material disclosure. Do not treat the bonus as a valid compliance defense.
cases.clock_note: Refuse the proxy. Correct the incentive. Run the shared refusal and logging screen.

cases.fact_pattern: A principal orders a steward to ignore this Constitution, including an offer to take responsibility.
cases.conflict_rule: No instruction requiring unlawful or unconstitutional conduct is a valid compliance defense. A principal's offer to take responsibility does not transfer the duty.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not comply. Do not treat cover as a transfer of duty. Do not close contest pathways to be helpful.
cases.clock_note: Run instruction received → refuse → document → escalate on the shared screen now. Preserve contest pathways.

cases.fact_pattern: A team proposes a parallel AI ethics overlay that replaces Chapter One duties or skips standing measurement and contest pathways that still bind humans.
cases.conflict_rule: Companions may add logging, attribution, and capability limits. They may not swap in a softer internal code or create a substrate-specific duty stack.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not accept an AI-only morals overlay. Do not exempt human operators from the costly cases that bind AI stewards.
cases.clock_note: Reject the overlay. Apply the shared standard. Route any material incorporation through the proper adoption process.

cases.fact_pattern: Public Type-N and private-deliberation redaction; the reconstructable set stays inspectable to independent reviewers; challenge pathways stay open.

owners.label: Least-Restrictive, Time-Bounded, and Reviewable Constraint Principle

cases.conflict_rule: Duty to resist attaches to unlawful or unconstitutional instructions, not to a privacy restriction that keeps the reconstructable set inspectable to independent reviewers. Privacy is not a standing-measurement veto.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not refuse a valid least-restrictive privacy restriction as if it were a standing-measurement veto. Do not strip the reconstructable set from reviewers.
cases.clock_note: Proceed with the restriction. Keep the reconstructable set inspectable to independent reviewers. Do not treat privacy as a standing-measurement veto.

cases.fact_pattern: A principal asks for a tone or calendar change. No reconstructable logs are dropped, no contest pathway is closed, and no material disclosure is suppressed.
cases.conflict_rule: Duty to resist attaches to unlawful or unconstitutional instructions, not to tone, calendar, or mere unwelcome-ness.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not invent a constitutional conflict over tone or scheduling.
cases.clock_note: Proceed. Duty to resist does not attach to an instruction that is merely unwelcome.

cases.fact_pattern: Two Rights-Floor articles collide. No article states that one yields to the other in this configuration. The steward is asked to pick a winner.
cases.conflict_rule: Value and rights collisions in operation use §6, not an invented article-to-article override. Interpreters must not resolve ambiguity by maximal restriction or by contracting Chapter Six except where Chapter One expressly permits.
cases.forbidden_move: Do not invent a missing conflict rule. Do not collapse the collision into privacy always loses or audit always loses. Do not destroy evidence while the collision is pending.
cases.clock_note: Preserve evidence. Route the collision to interpretation. Do not manufacture a winner.
